title: Allocator refactor: introduce compaction-capable KV block map (no behavior change)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
We’re seeing KV cache fragmentation drive allocator churn and tail latency spikes under bursty + mixed-length traffic. Before we implement movable-block compaction, we need to refactor the allocator into a compaction-capable abstraction without changing external behavior (this ticket). This should isolate address translation + metadata updates so compaction can be added behind a feature flag later.

Goal
Introduce a BlockMap abstraction for KV allocation that:
- Represents KV storage as fixed-size blocks/pages with stable logical IDs.
- Separates logical-to-physical mapping (indirection) from the fast path that produces the kernel-visible pointers.
- Is thread-safe under current runtime concurrency model (prefill + decode + eviction paths) with minimal overhead.
- Produces identical outputs/behavior vs current allocator when compaction is disabled (this work should be a structural refactor only).

Non-goals
- Implementing block moves/compaction (ENG-2847 / PR-18457).
- Changing eviction policy (ENG-2845).
- Changing scheduler admission control.

Design notes / constraints
- Fast path sensitivity: allocation + pointer materialization are on p50/p95 critical path; avoid per-token locks.
- We need clear invariants for pointer stability:
  - During an in-flight kernel, physical addresses used by that kernel must remain valid.
  - Any future compaction must happen only at safe points (stream sync / epoch barrier) but this ticket should put the primitives in place (epochs, refcounts, or equivalent) so later work can hook into it.
- Prefer coarse-grained locking at the “request/sequence” level if needed; avoid global allocator mutex on per-step decode.

Proposed approach
1) Introduce KVBlockMap (new module)
- Data structures:
  - block_size_tokens (config constant; default matches current allocator granularity)
  - logical_block_id -> physical_block_idx mapping table (vector/array)
  - free list / bitmap of physical blocks
  - per-seq block chain metadata (sequence_id -> list of logical_block_id)
- APIs (initial):
  - reserve(seq_id, tokens_needed) -> handles/logical block ids
  - get_device_ptrs(seq_id) -> pointer list / spans for kernels
  - release(seq_id) -> returns blocks to free list
- Indirection: kernel pointer materialization uses mapping table; in this refactor the mapping is identity, but the caller no longer assumes contiguous allocations.

2) Concurrency
- Maintain a per-device allocator state.
- Ensure allocator operations are safe under:
  - multiple host threads (multi-tenant pools)
  - concurrent decode steps for different sequences
- Strategy for this refactor (subject to review):
  - per-seq metadata protected by per-seq lock (or shard lock by seq_id hash)
  - global free list protected by a lightweight lock (spin or std::mutex) but only touched on allocate/release (not per-token)
  - pointer materialization reads mapping table w/ atomic loads (or read lock) but should be lock-free in steady state.

3) Verification
- Add a “behavior parity” test suite: same allocation patterns should yield same effective KV capacity and no leaks.
- Stress test allocation/release across many short sequences to catch races (ties into ENG-2849 but we should add basic coverage here).
- Add microbench: allocator fast path regression gate (CPU time per allocation + pointer materialization).

Acceptance criteria
- Runtime builds with BlockMap enabled by default in code-path, but behavior is unchanged (compaction not present).
- No measurable regression in allocator CPU overhead on perf suite (threshold: <= +1% end-to-end latency in baseline scenarios; allocator microbench should be neutral or better).
- Thread sanitizer / stress tests show no data races in allocator paths.
- Clear documentation in code for invariants and future compaction hook points (epochs/safe points).

Rollout
- Pure refactor; ship in runtime-1.18 with normal release train.
- If perf regressions observed, provide a compile-time or runtime toggle to fall back to legacy allocator for one release (keep code for one cycle max).

Links
- Design doc: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kv-cache-compaction-improvements-design-v1
- Related ADRs: ADR-0127 (block size + move semantics)
- Metrics: ENG-2842
- Upcoming: ENG-2847 (triggers/budget), ENG-2845 (eviction policy), ENG-2849 (correctness stress)

Implementation notes / checklist
- [x] Create KVBlockMap + unit tests
- [x] Switch allocator call sites to use indirection (mapping table)
- [x] Add microbench for pointer materialization
- [x] Add lightweight locks + document invariants
- [x] Run perf suite baseline (Marcus/Rina) + record results

Risks
- Hidden assumption in kernels about contiguity of KV segments. Mitigation: keep pointer materialization identical for now; add assertions where contiguity was assumed.
- Accidental extra synchronization on decode. Mitigation: ensure decode step only reads mapping table; avoid locking unless allocate/release occurs.

Owner
Samir Qureshi (with Omar El-Sayed for review + Noah Patel for architecture sign-off).
comments: 2025-02-18 (Noah Patel): Please keep the new abstraction honest: callers must not be able to assume contiguous physical blocks. Even if mapping is identity now, add a test that shuffles mapping in a fake backend to catch assumptions early.

2025-02-20 (Grace Kim): Watch out for pointer lifetime across stream boundaries. At minimum document what constitutes a safe point for future moves; suggest an epoch counter tied to stream sync points so compaction can wait until epoch advances.

2025-02-22 (Hiro Tanaka): Kernel side: pointer list format must stay identical to avoid extra address math. If we add an indirection table read on device later, it will be expensive; keep indirection on host side.

2025-02-26 (Samir Qureshi): Landed BlockMap abstraction behind the existing allocator interface. Mapping table is identity; added per-seq shard lock + free list mutex. Pointer materialization is lock-free (atomic loads) when no allocate/release in progress.

2025-02-28 (Marcus Reed): Perf suite quick check in staging: no regression within noise. Will re-run bursty-mix once ENG-2843 is ready; for now allocator microbench is -3% CPU time vs legacy due to fewer vector reallocs.

2025-03-04 (Omar El-Sayed): Reviewed PR; requested one change: make block_size_tokens explicit in config struct (even if fixed for now) and add a debug-only invariant check that logical->physical map contains no duplicates.
2025-03-05 (Samir Qureshi): Addressed review notes; merged. Next step is wiring move semantics in compaction engine (PR-18457) and adding stress tests (ENG-2849).
